video_title: Why Stablecoins Need to Move Beyond the Dollar
gist: Ripio CEO Sebastian Serrano explains why his firm issues six local-currency stablecoins (ARS, BRL, COP, MXN, CLP, PEN) rather than dollar coins, citing velocity, one-to-one ramps and DeFi composability. Early metrics are about 15 million supply growing roughly 30% monthly, with a thesis that tokenization is moving down from USD to the roughly 100 trillion dollars of non-USD money.

themes.theme: Local-currency stablecoins as the next tokenization wave

insights.claim: Ripio argues tokenization moves from the most liquid asset downward, so after USD stablecoins, equities and treasuries, tokenized local fiat currencies are the next layer; non-USD currencies total about 100 trillion dollars (roughly 5x the US figure, half of it China) versus about 0.002% tokenized today, with Ripio targeting 1%.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Frames a very large, almost untouched addressable market for non-USD stablecoins, though the 1% target is an aspiration, not a forecast of demand.

insights.claim: Roughly 1 to 1.5% of the 23 trillion US dollars is tokenized, and Serrano says the Treasury expects about 10% within a decade, giving a benchmark for how far local-currency tokenization could progress.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Gives an adoption-curve analog for local stablecoins; the Treasury figure is relayed secondhand.

insights.claim: Serrano says he would have rejected local stablecoins three years ago because the dollar is the asset people save in, but local-currency stablecoins have utility because people pay bills and sign contracts in local currency, not because anyone wants to hold them.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Demand for local stablecoins is payment and velocity driven, not savings driven, so investors should value them on turnover, not on balances.
insights.quote: Almost every contract is denominated in local currency.

insights.claim: Almost all stablecoin issuers target dollar-denominated coins, and Ripio says it knows of no one else pursuing its local-currency suite strategy, which it admits could mean it is very early or very wrong.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Low competition today, but also unproven demand; first-mover advantage depends on licenses and rails that others lack.

insights.claim: Ripio's six wrapped-fiat stablecoins (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Chile, Peru) launched November of last year; supply grew from about 800k to about 15 million dollars, growing roughly 30% month over month, with about 46,000 monthly active addresses.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Fast growth off a tiny base; 15 million supply is small, so scaling evidence is still ahead.

insights.claim: The entire local-stablecoin supply turns over weekly, with 10 to 15 million dollars or more of transfers per week, indicating extreme velocity relative to a roughly 15 million supply.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Velocity, not balance size, is the real usage signal; fee revenue may scale with turnover.

insights.claim: About a third of the local-currency stablecoin supply is deposited in Morpho vaults, and Uniswap swap counts doubled in the last month, mostly swaps under 200 dollars.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Shows DeFi composability is already being used, mostly by small retail-sized flows.

insights.claim: Ripio is currently the main LP across networks and pools for its local stablecoins; LPing a weak emerging-market currency against the dollar needs yields well above 3 to 4%, and competition for liquidity is expected to emerge.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Liquidity provision carries currency-depreciation risk, so margins may compress once competing LPs arrive.

insights.claim: Ripio's business model is to subsidize zero-fee one-to-one on and off ramps by managing the float, similar to how fintechs like Nubank give away onboarding and earn on credit.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Ramps are a loss leader; profits depend on float management and downstream services, so reserve yield and rates matter to margins.

insights.claim: Non-custodial wallets convert and retain poorly because their main call to action is buy, forcing 5 to 10 minutes of onboarding and then FX spread, so a Brazilian sending 1,000 reals ends with about 950 in ETH or USDC and loses money on first use.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Fixing first-deposit friction is a distribution lever for wallets; one-to-one ramps are the proposed solution.
insights.quote: your first experience using crypto is losing money.

insights.claim: Ripio's fix is a fintech-style deposit flow: the user sends 1,000 reals via Pix and receives 1,000 reals on chain, with zero onboarding fees, and Ripio says this produced strong conversion and now powers World App, Coinbase Wallet and MiniPay, with PicPay starting.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Wallet distribution partners are the growth channel, and about 10 fintechs and wallets integrated in the last quarter.

insights.claim: Serrano says on-ramps are a loss leader at exchanges and fintechs generally, with money made on exchange fees, float or credit, which explains why on-ramp-only startups have struggled.
insights.speaker: Host and Sebastian Serrano
insights.so_what: Pure on-ramp businesses lack a profit engine; look for the monetizing layer behind the ramp.

themes.theme: Use cases: DeFi inversion, FX, remittances, prediction markets

insights.claim: DeFi lending is backwards for emerging markets: users hold dollars as savings but protocols like Morpho and Aave have them post BTC or ETH to borrow dollars, whereas they should post USDC or USDT and borrow local currency, which requires local currency stablecoins on chain.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Opens a lending product for savers: dollar collateral, local-currency loans, demand for local-currency liquidity in DeFi.

insights.claim: On-chain FX is already cheaper than incumbents: sending 1,000 reals to Argentina via Wise yields about 285,000 pesos while Uniswap swapping the Ripio real and peso tokens yields about 315,000, roughly a 10% difference.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Cross-border corridors between neighbors with hard-to-hold treasuries may be the first to move on chain; the comparison is a point-in-time anecdote.

insights.claim: Wise transfers from Brazil to Argentina typically take a day and cost around 10% on the exchange rate, and incumbents wire via the US and back, while many Argentine fintechs already use a stablecoin sandwich behind the scenes for Pix payments.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Stablecoins are already embedded invisibly in LatAm payments, so adoption may not look like crypto adoption.

insights.claim: Any localized crypto product, such as a prediction market for Boca versus River, needs local-currency collateral, so local stablecoins are a prerequisite for localizing apps like Polymarket.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: A speculative use case; no localized prediction market has taken off yet.

themes.theme: LatAm market structure and Ripio's position

insights.claim: Argentines and Venezuelans track the peso-dollar rate by memory and save leftover income in dollar stablecoins as protection, whereas Brazilians barely track the rate; crypto in Argentina is used for safe haven rather than speculation.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Demand for stablecoins in the region is defensive and sticky, differing by country.

insights.claim: Brazilian bonds pay 13 to 15% with a stable real, and Argentine pesos yield about 25%, and Argentines are buying Ripio's Brazilian real token to run carry trades, so higher local yields are a draw for tokenized local currencies.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Yield-bearing local-currency tokens could attract global carry capital; currency risk remains.

insights.claim: Pix, CVU, Breve and similar real-time payment networks outperform US rails, Pix volume exceeds card payments in Brazil, and Chile, Peru and Uruguay lack such networks but are copying Brazil, so local stablecoin connectivity to these rails is an infrastructure moat.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Licenses and bank connections, not the token itself, are the defensible asset, which favors licensed incumbents over API aggregators.

insights.claim: Ripio is crypto-as-a-service provider for Mercado Libre's Mercado Pago, reaching about 35 million B2B2C users and 100 to 200 transactions per second via its loyalty token, and serves most Argentine brokers' crypto offerings.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Large embedded distribution gives the wrapped-fiat suite built-in channels.

insights.claim: Serrano says central banks and regulators align with local stablecoins because reserves buy government debt, while banks are likely to dislike them as DeFi pays more on deposits; at 0.001% share it is not yet on bank radars.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Regulatory pushback risk comes later, from banks losing deposit relationships, not from sovereigns.

insights.claim: Ripio's stablecoins are on 10 EVM chains, with Ethereum mainnet largest by AUM and heavy activity on Base, Celo and World Chain (about 6 million active users in the region), and it plans to stay chain-agnostic, with no Solana, relying on its EVM expertise.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Distribution is multi-chain, so value accrues to the issuer and rails rather than any single chain.

insights.claim: AMMs will serve small FX trades of 200 to 1,000 dollars, while larger FX flows will need order books like Hyperliquid and RFQ systems like StableFX or Celo-based protocols, and Ripio is testing Uniswap hooks with price references.
insights.speaker: Sebastian Serrano (Ripio CEO)
insights.so_what: Institutional-size FX on chain depends on RFQ and order-book infrastructure; price discovery is not the bottleneck, since FX markets have reference prices.
